title: Maps from a module of finite presentation into a directed colimit factor through a stage, on a qcqs scheme (Stacks 01BS)
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. An $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ is *of finite presentation* if every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ with an exact sequence $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_U\to0$ of $\mathcal O_U$-modules (Stacks, Modules, Definition 01BN). Let $I$ be a directed set, $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_{i'i})_{i\le i'}$ a system of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over $I$ with a colimit $(\mathcal F,(c_i:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F)_i)$ in the category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and $\mathcal G$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite presentation. Then the canonical map $\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F_i)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$, $g\mapsto c_i\circ g$ on the $i$-th term, is bijective: every $\mathcal O_X$-linear $h:\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ is $c_i\circ g$ for some $i\in I$ and some $\mathcal O_X$-linear $g:\mathcal G\to\mathcal F_i$, and if $c_i\circ g=c_{i'}\circ g'$ then $\varphi_{i''i}\circ g=\varphi_{i''i'}\circ g'$ for some $i''\ge i,i'$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BS (lemma-finite-presentation-quasi-compact-colimit, line 3818; proof via Lemma lemma-hom-finite-presentation-colimit, line 3759, and Sheaves, Lemma 009F); its hypothesis (3) (a cofinal system of finite open coverings with quasi-compact pairwise intersections) holds on a qcqs scheme by finite affine open coverings and Schemes, Lemma 01KO (lemma-characterize-quasi-separated, schemes.tex line 4125)

proof.text: *Step 1 (the Hom sheaves).* For each $i$ let $\mathcal H_i=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F_i)$ and let $\mathcal H=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ be the sheaf Homs on the opens of $X$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom]: $\mathcal H_i(U)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal G|_U,\mathcal F_i|_U)$, sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $i\le i'$ let $\mathcal H_i\to\mathcal H_{i'}$ be $\psi\mapsto\varphi_{i'i}|_U\circ\psi$ and let $\gamma_i:\mathcal H_i\to\mathcal H$ be $\psi\mapsto c_i|_U\circ\psi$ ($\psi\in\mathcal H_i(U)$). These are $\mathcal O_X$-linear maps of sheaves (postcomposition with an $\mathcal O_U$-linear map is $\mathcal O_X(U)$-linear for the module structure of [def-pur-sheaf-hom] and commutes with restriction to smaller opens), $(\mathcal H_i)$ is a system over $I$ because $\varphi_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\varphi_{i''i'}\varphi_{i'i}=\varphi_{i''i}$, and $\gamma_{i'}\circ(\mathcal H_i\to\mathcal H_{i'})=\gamma_i$ because $c_{i'}\varphi_{i'i}=c_i$. On global sections, $\mathcal H_i(X)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F_i)$ and $\mathcal H(X)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ ('by construction', Stacks), the transition maps are $g\mapsto\varphi_{i'i}\circ g$ and $\gamma_{i,X}$ is $g\mapsto c_i\circ g$. So the map of the statement is the map $\varinjlim_i\mathcal H_i(X)\to\mathcal H(X)$ induced by the $\gamma_{i,X}$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BS (lemma-finite-presentation-quasi-compact-colimit, line 3818), proof, first sentences ('Set H = Hom(G, colim F_i) and H_i = Hom(G, F_i). Recall that Hom_X(G,F) = Γ(X,H) ... by construction'); Section 01CM (section-internal-hom), the definition of the sheaf Hom (line 3504)

proof.text: *Step 2 ($\mathcal H=\varinjlim\mathcal H_i$).* Since $\mathcal G$ is of finite presentation and $(\mathcal F,(c_i))$ is a colimit of the $\mathcal F_i$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, the system $(\mathcal H_i)_{i\in I}$ has a colimit $(\mathcal H',(d_i)_i)$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ and the unique $\mathcal O_X$-linear $u:\mathcal H'\to\mathcal H$ with $u\circ d_i=\gamma_i$ is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-hom-finite-presentation-colimit] (Stacks: 'By Lemma 0GMV we have H = colim H_i').

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BS (lemma-finite-presentation-quasi-compact-colimit, line 3818), proof ('By Lemma lemma-hom-finite-presentation-colimit we have H = colim H_i')

proof.text: *Step 3 (the covering hypothesis of 01BS holds on $X$).* Since $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $X$ has a cofinal system of open coverings $X=\bigcup_{j\in J}U_j$ with $J$ finite and all $U_j\cap U_{j'}$ quasi-compact, namely its finite affine open coverings [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-cofinal-finite-coverings]. This is hypothesis (3) of Stacks 01BS, which is how the qcqs hypothesis of the statement enters (Stacks, Remark 01BT/Sheaves Example 009G: quasi-compactness of $X$ alone does not suffice).

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BS, hypothesis (3), and Remark remark-condition-necessary after it; Schemes, Lemmas 01IT and 01KO

proof.text: *Step 4 (global sections of the colimit, Sheaves 009F).* By [lem-weil-pbc-module-directed-colimit-underlying-sets], the underlying sheaf of sets of $\mathcal H'$ with the maps $d_i$ is a colimit of the underlying sheaves of sets of the $\mathcal H_i$ in the category of sheaves of sets on $X$. By Step 3 the open $U=X$ satisfies the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-sheaves-directed-colimit-sections](2), so the map $\Psi_X:\varinjlim_i\mathcal H_i(X)\to\mathcal H'(X)$ induced by the $d_{i,X}$ is bijective. Since $u$ is an isomorphism (Step 2), $u_X:\mathcal H'(X)\to\mathcal H(X)$ is bijective, and $u_X\circ\Psi_X$ is the map induced by the $u_X\circ d_{i,X}=\gamma_{i,X}$, i.e. by Step 1 the canonical map $\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F_i)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$, $g\mapsto c_i\circ g$. It is therefore bijective.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BS (lemma-finite-presentation-quasi-compact-colimit, line 3818), proof ('Thus the lemma follows from Sheaves, Lemma 009F'); literature/stacks-project/sheaves.tex Lemma 009F (4)

proof.text: *Step 5 (the two explicit clauses).* The directed colimit of the sets $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F_i)$ is the disjoint union of these sets modulo $(i,g)\sim(i',g')$ iff $\varphi_{i''i}\circ g=\varphi_{i''i'}\circ g'$ for some $i''\ge i,i'$ (an equivalence relation since $I$ is directed), with the coprojections $g\mapsto[(i,g)]$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Surjectivity of the map of Step 4 says every $h$ is $c_i\circ g$ for some $i$ and $g$; injectivity says that $c_i\circ g=c_{i'}\circ g'$ implies $[(i,g)]=[(i',g')]$, i.e. $\varphi_{i''i}\circ g=\varphi_{i''i'}\circ g'$ for some $i''\ge i,i'$.

lean.statement: theorem hom_directedColimit_of_isFinitePresentation (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (I : Type u) [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (D : I ⥤ X.Modules) (c : Cocone D) (hc : IsColimit c) (G : X.Modules) [SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation.{u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) G] : (∀ h : G ⟶ c.pt, ∃ (i : I) (g : G ⟶ D.obj i), g ≫ c.ι.app i = h) ∧ (∀ (i j : I) (g : G ⟶ D.obj i) (g' : G ⟶ D.obj j), g ≫ c.ι.app i = g' ≫ c.ι.app j → ∃ (k : I) (hik : i ≤ k) (hjk : j ≤ k), g ≫ D.map (homOfLE hik) = g' ≫ D.map (homOfLE hjk))
